 Sam Claflin, the actor who traded the heartthrob roles for damaged men
 Photo: Unknown authorUnknown author / CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons — Wikimedia Commons 
 By 
 Penelope H. Fritz 
 5 min read 
 Add us on Google 
 Sam Claflin Photo: dalekhelen / CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons Born June 27, 1986
 Ipswich, Suffolk, England, United Kingdom 
 Occupation Actor 
 Known for Me Before You, The Hunger Games: Catching Fire, Love, Rosie 
 The first thing Hollywood asked of Sam Claflin, more or less, was to take his shirt off. He was the young missionary who falls for a mermaid in a Pirates of the Caribbean sequel, then the bronzed victor who strolls up to Katniss Everdeen offering a sugar cube, and for a while the industry treated his torso as the main argument for casting him. Claflin has since said that the attention fed a body dysmorphia he still lives with. The more interesting story is what he did with the leverage. He spent the next decade collecting men who are hard to love: a venomous Oxford toff, a colonial officer who commits atrocities, Britain’s most notorious interwar fascist. Even his romantic leads tend to arrive broken.
 He grew up in Norwich, the third of four brothers, the son of a finance officer and a teaching assistant, and for most of his childhood the plan was football. He trained with Norwich City’s school of excellence until a broken ankle ended any thought of playing professionally. A teacher who had watched him in a play at Costessey High School, backed by his parents, steered him toward drama instead.
 Claflin, who was born in Ipswich on 27 June 1986, studied performing arts at Norwich City College and graduated from the London Academy of Music and Dramatic Art in 2009. Television came first and came quickly: a young nobleman in The Pillars of the Earth , the younger Logan Mountstuart in Any Human Heart , and the Manchester United prodigy Duncan Edwards, who died of his injuries after the Munich air disaster, in the BBC drama United .
 Then the franchises found him. In Pirates of the Caribbean: On Stranger Tides (2011) he played Philip Swift, the earnest clergyman of the voyage, and a year later he was William, the childhood friend with a crossbow, in Snow White and the Huntsman . In August 2012 Lionsgate announced him as Finnick Odair, and from The Hunger Games: Catching Fire (2013) through The Hunger Games: Mockingjay – Part 2 (2015) he turned a character introduced as pure flirtation into the saga’s most quietly wounded survivor.
 What he chose between those blockbusters is more revealing. In Lone Scherfig’s The Riot Club (2014) he played Alistair Ryle, the most poisonous member of an Oxford dining society, making entitlement look repellent and, now and then, fragile. The same year he was the hopeless best friend in Love, Rosie opposite Lily Collins , a film critics shrugged at and audiences adopted. In Thea Sharrock’s Me Before You (2016) he was Will Traynor, a wealthy young man paralysed in an accident, opposite Emilia Clarke. Saul Dibb’s Journey’s End (2017) cast him as Captain Stanhope, a company commander in the trenches holding himself together with whisky, and in Baltasar Kormákur’s Adrift (2018) he was the sailor whose injuries leave Shailene Woodley ‘s character steering a wrecked yacht across the Pacific.
 The sharpest turn came with Jennifer Kent’s The Nightingale (2018), set in colonial Tasmania, where he played Hawkins, a British officer whose violence drives the entire film. It remains the darkest work on his résumé, and the clearest sign that he was willing to use a pleasant face against the audience. The BBC’s Peaky Blinders then gave him Oswald Mosley, the leader of the British Union of Fascists, across its last two seasons, a soft-spoken menace opposite Cillian Murphy ‘s Tommy Shelby. In Enola Holmes (2020) he became the starchier of the two Holmes brothers, a Mycroft who mostly wants his sister in a finishing school.
 His public image has not always kept pace with those choices, and some of the friction is his own account of it. Me Before You became a commercial hit and the most contested film he has made. Disability campaigners from Not Dead Yet UK picketed the London premiere and called it a “disability snuff movie”, objecting to a story in which a paralysed man decides life is not worth living, and to the casting of a non-disabled actor in the part. A promotional online Q&A in his name was flooded with hostile questions. Claflin, meanwhile, was being marketed as a heartthrob at the very moment, by his own later telling, he was struggling with how he looked. “There’s this Hollywood assumption that it’s the men with the six packs who sell the movie,” he told Variety. He first spoke about body dysmorphia in 2025 and returned to it on Fearne Cotton’s Happy Place podcast in February 2026, describing it as a daily struggle and admitting he remains “incredibly insecure”. The actor sold as the easy pin-up was, it turns out, the person in the room least convinced by the poster.
 Streaming made him a leading man on his own terms. In Daisy Jones & the Six (2023) for Prime Video he played Billy Dunne, a 1970s frontman whose sobriety and marriage keep colliding with his ego, and he sang on Aurora , the fictional band’s album, which was released for real. The role earned him a Golden Globe nomination. Bille August ‘s eight-part The Count of Monte Cristo , an Italian-French production with Jeremy Irons as the Abbé Faria, gave him Edmond Dantès; it aired in Italy from January 2025 and reached American audiences in March 2026. Prime Video’s Harlan Coben’s Lazarus , launched in October 2025 with Bill Nighy as his father, split critics. On film there were the horror film Bagman (2024) and Barnaby Roper’s crime thriller All the Devils Are Here (2025), with Eddie Marsan and Rory Kinnear.
 This year began with Vanished , a four-part MGM+ thriller in which he played Tom Parker, the boyfriend who disappears from a train to Arles and leaves Kaley Cuoco ‘s archaeologist to discover who he really was. Reviews were mixed, but the role suited his particular gift for men whose charm hides a second life.
 Claflin met the actress Laura Haddock at an audition for My Week with Marilyn in 2011. They married in July 2013, had a son and a daughter, and announced their separation in August 2019. Since 2025 he has been in a relationship with Dar Zuzovsky, whom he met on the set of Vanished ; the couple appeared together at the London premiere of his new film.
 That film is Ebenezer: A Christmas Carol , Ti West ‘s gothic take on Dickens, which Paramount opens in American cinemas on 13 November 2026 with Johnny Depp as Scrooge. Claflin plays Fred, the nephew who keeps inviting the old miser to Christmas dinner after years of refusals. It reunites him with Depp fifteen years after On Stranger Tides , and it hands the actor who built a career on cads the most stubbornly decent man in the book.
